name: how to read this page, answered on the page
old: Set a job below. It gets quoted twice: with memory, and with none.
new:
Set a job below. It gets quoted twice: with memory, and with none.
How to read this page
What this tab proves
Every number here is produced from two transactions that really settled on Base Sepolia. Both memories hold them, each receipt links to the block explorer, and the same engine is run twice at the same starting numbers: once with those receipts and once with none. Any difference between the two columns is memory and nothing else.
What the simulator may invent, and what it may not
The simulator lets you suppose a history that never happened and asks the real engine what these two would then agree. It signs nothing and touches no wallet. What it may not invent is how an outcome is read: those readings were learned from outcomes that did settle, and an outcome neither memory has learned to read is refused by name rather than scored as harmless.
Why a receipt is required before memory changes
An agent that can be told a bad outcome happened is an agent anyone can slander. Memory is only ever written from a receipt this build has verified against the chain, so an intention that was never executed is never treated as misconduct.
Included, and confirmed
Included means a block holds it, about ten seconds in. The agent reads the receipt, the sender, the logs and the contract’s own state at that block, and requires all of them to agree. Confirmed means Base can no longer reverse it, roughly two minutes later. A wallet is freed by the first. Memory may only be written from the second, because a memory that could be withdrawn would leave every deal signed in between committed to a history that no longer exists.
What can refuse a deal before anything is signed
Of the four starting numbers, one can break a deal on its own: no seller will ever stake more than half the price, so ask for more and there is nothing to negotiate. The other three cannot, because both sides scale with the price, the seller needs five minutes or your figure whichever is smaller, and the buyer accepts a fraction of whatever wait you set. Everything else that refuses is history, and it always traces back to the record of the side being refused.
